questions.question_text: In the New York Longitudinal Study (Thomas and Chess 1984):

options.text: The most stable trait was 'approach or withdrawal to novelty', which seems the same thing as the extroversion–introversion polarity
Most children (65%) could be categorized into three broad groupings: easy, difficult and slow to warm up
Those exposed to parental conflict at age 3 were more likely to have poor adult social adjustment
'Poor fit' between a child's temperament and parental /teacher expectations was a risk factor for child maladjustment
All of the above

correct_answer.text: All of the above

correct_answers.text: All of the above

questions.explanation: Children of 'difficult' temperament at age 3 (especially those exposed to parental conflict) were more likely to have poor adult social adjustment. 'Poor fit' can be reduced by counselling and education.

questions.question_text: Freud's concepts include all of the following, except:

options.text: The unconscious mind must exist because people say and do more than they are 'aware of' or 'mean to'
Every mental event is affected by previous ones
The selective unconscious 'forgetting' of events too painful or objectionable to the conscious mind
At some early stage the infant gets the idea of being fed from 'out there' (by the 'good breast'), but when the infant is hungry the 'out there' must be holding off (the 'bad breast')
From birth into the second year, an infant has both libidinal and aggressive drives centred on 'oral eroticism', e.g. sucking, and 'oral sadism', e.g. biting

correct_answer.text: At some early stage the infant gets the idea of being fed from 'out there' (by the 'good breast'), but when the infant is hungry the 'out there' must be holding off (the 'bad breast')

correct_answers.text: At some early stage the infant gets the idea of being fed from 'out there' (by the 'good breast'), but when the infant is hungry the 'out there' must be holding off (the 'bad breast')

questions.explanation: 'Good breast /bad breast' is a concept proposed by Melanie Klein. That every mental event is affected by previous ones is psychic determinism. Forgetting events too painful or objectionable to the conscious mind is repression.

questions.question_text: All of the following terms are associated with Freud, except:

options.text: Transitional object
Oedipal complex
Electra complex
Introjection
Pleasure principle

correct_answer.text: Transitional object

correct_answers.text: Transitional object

questions.explanation: The term 'transitional object' is associated with Donald Winnicott (1896–1971).

questions.question_text: Behavioural dimensions indicating inborn temperamental attributes include:

options.text: Activity level
Rhythmicity
Approach or withdrawal
Adaptability
All of the above

correct_answer.text: All of the above

correct_answers.text: All of the above

questions.explanation: Thomas and Chess identified nine behavioural dimensions. The others include intensity of reaction, threshold of responsiveness, quality of mood, attention span and persistence, and distractibility.

questions.question_text: Regarding attachment, which of the following statements is true?

options.text: Bonding is the same as attachment
Mary Ainsworth described attachment behaviour
John Bowlby described the sequential pattern of protest, despair and detachment as the infant's response to separation from the caretaker
Attachment behaviour starts at 6 months after birth
Inanimate objects cannot provide a secure base effect

correct_answer.text: John Bowlby described the sequential pattern of protest, despair and detachment as the infant's response to separation from the caretaker

correct_answers.text: John Bowlby described the sequential pattern of protest, despair and detachment as the infant's response to separation from the caretaker

questions.explanation: Bonding is the intense emotional and psychological relationship a mother develops with her baby. Attachment is the relationship the baby develops with its caregivers. Bowlby described attachment behaviour and Ainsworth developed it. Attachment behaviour starts from birth. Inanimate objects can provide a secure base effect; ones doing so were described by Winnicott as transitional objects.

questions.question_text: Stranger anxiety:

options.text: Appears in the first month
Is more likely to occur in babies exposed to a variety of carers
Is identical to separation anxiety
Is fully established by 8 months
Does not occur when the infant is in the mother's arms

correct_answer.text: Is fully established by 8 months

correct_answers.text: Is fully established by 8 months

questions.explanation: Stranger anxiety appears around 26 weeks, more commonly in babies exposed to a single carer. Separation anxiety occurs at between 10 and 18 weeks and is related to stranger anxiety but is not identical.

questions.question_text: In learning theory, all of the following are true, except:

options.text: Drugs of abuse can act as a positive reinforcement at the biological level
Negative reinforcement can exacerbate the avoidance response in phobic avoidance states
In cognitive learning, more information leads to more effective and predictable outcomes
Extinction occurs as part of stimulus generalization
A prison sentence that follows long after the crime has been committed may not affect future criminal behaviour

correct_answer.text: Extinction occurs as part of stimulus generalization

correct_answers.text: Extinction occurs as part of stimulus generalization

questions.explanation: Extinction is the gradual disappearance of a conditioned stimulus; generalization is the process whereby the same response is evoked by a similar stimulus.

questions.question_text: Piaget's developmental stage corresponding to Freud's latency stage is the:

options.text: Sensorimotor stage
Formal operational stage
Preoperational stage
Concrete operational stage
Formal operations stage

correct_answer.text: Concrete operational stage

correct_answers.text: Concrete operational stage

questions.explanation: The concrete operational stage is between 7 and 11 years, when egocentric thought is replaced by operational thought and critical achievements are mastering the concepts of conservation and reversibility.

questions.question_text: In the management of psychosis, one of the benefits of psychodynamic understanding is that:

options.text: It helps to identify psychological stressors
It helps to identify personal significance in psychotic symptoms
It helps to clarify underlying vulnerability
It is useful in family meetings in which the aim is to understand the stresses and strains families face
All of the above

correct_answer.text: All of the above

correct_answers.text: All of the above

questions.explanation: Psychodynamic understanding also reveals the psychodynamic mechanisms operating in psychosis to avoid painful realities. It informs the phasing of recovery and suggests steps to tackle underlying vulnerability, thus contributing to relapse prevention.

questions.question_text: According to the psychoanalytic theory of depression:

options.text: Mourning and depression are types of biopsychological reactions to loss
The self undergoes an alteration through becoming identified with the lost object
Hostility is turned inward
The superego is coloured by the individual's own hostile and envious feelings
All of the above

correct_answer.text: All of the above

correct_answers.text: All of the above

questions.explanation: Emotional ambivalence deriving from early childhood relationships and losses is crucial.

questions.question_text: Which of the following is characteristic of attachment bonds?

options.text: Attachment bonds are not persistent
Attachment bonds involve a specific figure who is interchangeable
The relationship within the dyad is emotionally not significant
The individual wishes to maintain proximity to or contact with the attachment figure
The individual does not feel distress at involuntary separation from the attachment figure

correct_answer.text: The individual wishes to maintain proximity to or contact with the attachment figure

correct_answers.text: The individual wishes to maintain proximity to or contact with the attachment figure

questions.explanation: Attachment bonds are persistent; the specific figure is not interchangeable; the relationship within the dyad is emotionally significant; the individual feels distress at involuntary separation.

questions.question_text: According to Freud's theory of personality development, all of the following statements are true, except:

options.text: Excessive oral gratification or deprivation can result in libidinal fixations that lead to pathological traits like excessive optimism, narcissism, pessimism and demandingness
Anal eroticism and fixation on its defences may create maladaptive character traits like orderliness, obstinacy, stubbornness and parsimony
In the urethral stage, the main issues involve castration anxiety in males and penis envy in females
Excess of inner control in the latency stage can lead to premature closure of personality development and precocious elaboration of obsessive character traits
The genital stage involves partial reopening, reworking and reintegrating of all previous unsuccessful resolutions and fixations

correct_answer.text: In the urethral stage, the main issues involve castration anxiety in males and penis envy in females

correct_answers.text: In the urethral stage, the main issues involve castration anxiety in males and penis envy in females

questions.explanation: In the urethral stage, the issues are urethral performance and loss of control; in the phallic stage, the main issues are castration anxiety in males and penis envy in females.

questions.question_text: Narcissistic defences include:

options.text: Projection
Introjection
Regression
Displacement
Sublimation

correct_answer.text: Projection

correct_answers.text: Projection

questions.explanation: Other narcissistic defences are denial and distortion; immature defences include acting out, blocking, hypochondriasis, introjection, passive aggressive behaviour, regression, schizoid fantasy and somatization.

questions.question_text: Neurotic defences include:

options.text: Intellectualization
Rationalization
Reaction formation
Displacement
All of the above

correct_answer.text: All of the above

correct_answers.text: All of the above

questions.explanation: Other neurotic defences include controlling, externalization, inhibition, isolation, dissociation, repression and sexualization.

questions.question_text: Mature defences include:

options.text: Altruism
Anticipation
Asceticism
Humour
All of the above

correct_answer.text: All of the above

correct_answers.text: All of the above

questions.explanation: Mature defences also include sublimation and suppression.

questions.question_text: In psychoanalytic theory, all of the following are true, except:

options.text: Neurotic symptoms develop as a failure of repression
It emphasizes the importance of superego formation in the construction of character
Exaggerated development of certain character traits at the expense of others leads to personality disorders
The expulsion of the drives or wishes from conscious awareness through repression or other defence mechanisms makes those drives less powerful and influential
Traumatic events that seem to threaten survival may break through defences when the ego has been weakened

correct_answer.text: The expulsion of the drives or wishes from conscious awareness through repression or other defence mechanisms makes those drives less powerful and influential

correct_answers.text: The expulsion of the drives or wishes from conscious awareness through repression or other defence mechanisms makes those drives less powerful and influential

questions.explanation: The expulsion of the drives or wishes does not make them less powerful or influential; as a result, the unconscious tendencies fight their way back to consciousness (e.g. the disguised neurotic symptoms).

questions.question_text: All of the following are true about Jung's personality theory, except:

options.text: It rejects Freud's concept of the unconscious
Archetypes are described as representational images and configurations with universal symbolic meanings
Complexes develop as emotionally toned ideas
A major developmental goal in adult life is individualization
Anima refers to a man's undeveloped femininity and animus refers to a woman's undeveloped masculinity

correct_answer.text: It rejects Freud's concept of the unconscious

correct_answers.text: It rejects Freud's concept of the unconscious

questions.explanation: Jung expanded Freud's concept of the unconscious by describing collective unconsciousness as consisting of all humankind's common, shared mythological and symbolic past. This includes archetypes and complexes.

questions.question_text: All of the following statements are true about superego development in the psychoanalytic theory of personality development, except:

options.text: Superego is developed through identification with parents
Superego contains the individual's moral conscience
Superego anxiety occurs after the resolution of the oedipal complex
Superego develops before the child enters the oedipal stage
The scrutiny activities of superego occur largely unconsciously

correct_answer.text: Superego develops before the child enters the oedipal stage

correct_answers.text: Superego develops before the child enters the oedipal stage

questions.explanation: Superego is not formed until the oedipal complex is resolved and superego anxiety occurs around that time. The superego initially is the internalization of parental standards and values that include the ego ideal (what one should do) and moral conscience (what one should not do).

questions.question_text: According to the stages of separation individualization proposed by Margaret Mahler, normal rapprochement includes all of the following, except:

options.text: It occurs between 18 and 24 months
Children realize their helplessness and dependence
The need for independence alternates with the need for closeness
Children move away from their mother and come back for reassurance
Children gradually comprehend and are readily reassured by the presence of their mother and other important people

correct_answer.text: Children gradually comprehend and are readily reassured by the presence of their mother and other important people

correct_answers.text: Children gradually comprehend and are readily reassured by the presence of their mother and other important people

questions.explanation: Children gradually comprehend and are readily reassured by the presence of their mother and other important people in the stage of object constancy, at between 2 and 5 years.

questions.question_text: Regarding temperament, which of the following statements is true?

options.text: The concept of parental fit does not take account of the temperamental characteristics of the child
Thomas and Chess used the term 'goodness to fit' to characterize the harmonious and consonant interaction between a mother and a child
According to Bates, temperament concepts cannot be defined as the patterns of surface behaviour
The neural basis of temperament is thought to emerge from the cerebellum
Characteristics of temperament in infants and preschool children do not predict adjustment in middle childhood and adolescence

correct_answer.text: Thomas and Chess used the term 'goodness to fit' to characterize the harmonious and consonant interaction between a mother and a child

correct_answers.text: Thomas and Chess used the term 'goodness to fit' to characterize the harmonious and consonant interaction between a mother and a child

questions.explanation: Parental fit takes account of the temperamental characteristics of both parent and child. According to Bates, temperament concepts can be defined at three levels: as patterns of surface behaviour, as a pattern of nervous system response and as having inborn genetic roots. The neural basis of temperament is thought to emerge from the limbic structures, the association cortex and the motor cortical areas. Characteristics of temperament in infants and preschool children predict adjustment in middle childhood and adolescence.

questions.question_text: In the preschool period:

options.text: Children do not understand that there may be more than one point of view to a moral issue
A problem may result if the needs of a newborn baby prevent the mother from attending to a first-born child's needs
By the age of 4, children are usually able to engage in cooperative play
Imaginary companions most often appear in the preschool years
All of the above

correct_answer.text: All of the above

correct_answers.text: All of the above

questions.explanation: Children aged 3–6 are aware of their genitalia, and the differences between the sexes. Sibling rivalry appears, and growth can be traced through their drawings.

questions.question_text: Regarding adoption, all of the following statements are true, except:

options.text: Adoptive parents most often tell their children of their status between the ages of 2 and 4 years
Emotional and behavioural disorders have been reported to be higher among adopted than non-adopted children
The later the age of adoption, the lower is the incidence and the less severe are any behavioural problems
An adopted child may split two sets of parents into good and bad parents
Forty per cent of adopted children are born to mothers aged between 15 and 19 years

correct_answer.text: The later the age of adoption, the lower is the incidence and the less severe are any behavioural problems

correct_answers.text: The later the age of adoption, the lower is the incidence and the less severe are any behavioural problems

questions.explanation: The later the age of adoption, the higher is the incidence and the more severe are any behavioural problems.

questions.question_text: Rutter's observations about parenting styles include all of the following, except:

options.text: The authoritarian style leads to low self-esteem and social withdrawal in children
The indulgent–permissive style leads to low self-reliance and aggression in children
The indulgent–neglectful style leads to low self-esteem and aggression in children
The authoritative–reciprocal style leads to low self-reliance and impaired self-control in children
Firm rules and shared decision-making is the style most likely to result in self-reliance, self-esteem and a sense of social responsibility

correct_answer.text: The authoritative–reciprocal style leads to low self-reliance and impaired self-control in children

correct_answers.text: The authoritative–reciprocal style leads to low self-reliance and impaired self-control in children

questions.explanation: The authoritative–reciprocal style characterized by firm rules and shared decision-making is the style most likely to result in self-reliance, self-esteem and a sense of social responsibility.

questions.question_text: In Erikson's stages of the life cycle, which of the following statements is true about the psychopathological outcomes associated with each stage if it is not mastered successfully?

options.text: Basic mistrust is a major contribution to the development of schizoid personality disorder
If shame and doubt dominate over autonomy, obsessive personality develops
Excessive guilt between the ages of 3 and 5 years is associated with the development of schizophrenia
In stage 4, development of inferiority can lead to severe work inhibitions and feelings of inadequacy in adult life
Disorders during the stage of identity versus role diffusion include conduct disorder and psychotic disorders

correct_answer.text: Excessive guilt between the ages of 3 and 5 years is associated with the development of schizophrenia

correct_answers.text: Excessive guilt between the ages of 3 and 5 years is associated with the development of schizophrenia

questions.explanation: Excessive guilt in children aged between 3 and 5 years is associated with the development of generalized anxiety disorders and phobia. In stage 6, persons with schizoid personality remain isolated; stage 7 features increased use of alcohol; stage 8 is characterized by a severe depressive episode.

questions.question_text: Which of the following names is not paired with the correct term in the study of personality disorders?

options.text: Rush–Moral derangement
Pinel–Manie sans de ´lire
Kraepelin–Moral insanity
Henderson–Psychopathic states
Cleckley–Sociopathy

correct_answer.text: Kraepelin–Moral insanity

correct_answers.text: Kraepelin–Moral insanity

questions.explanation: Kraepelin first defined the psychopathic personality and Prichard first described moral insanity.

questions.question_text: All of the following are true about personality theories, except:

options.text: Eysenck's approach was categorical rather than dimensional
Normothetic theories are based on studies of populations
Ideographic theories relate to individual uniqueness
Kelly's personal constructs, being unconscious, are formed at earlier developmental stages
Bannister's Repertory Grid can be used to measure formal thought disorder

correct_answer.text: Eysenck's approach was categorical rather than dimensional

correct_answers.text: Eysenck's approach was categorical rather than dimensional

questions.explanation: Using factor analysis, Eysenck identified the following personality traits: neuroticism/stability; extroversion/introversion; psychoticism /stability; intelligence.

questions.question_text: Regarding genetic and environmental factors that contribute to personality disorders, all of the following statements are true, except:

options.text: Among monozygotic twins the concordance for personality disorders is several times that among dizygotic twins
Research shows that there is a difference in concordance for personality disorders in monozygotic twins reared together and apart
Cluster A personality disorders are more common in the biological relatives of patients with schizophrenia
Depression is common in the family backgrounds of patients with borderline personality disorder
There is more association between schizotypal personality disorder and schizophrenia than with schizoid personality disorder and schizophrenia

correct_answer.text: Research shows that there is a difference in concordance for personality disorders in monozygotic twins reared together and apart

correct_answers.text: Research shows that there is a difference in concordance for personality disorders in monozygotic twins reared together and apart

questions.explanation: One study has shown that there is no difference in concordance for personality disorders in monozygotic twins reared together and apart.

questions.question_text: Regarding biological factors that contribute to personality disorders, all of the following statements are true, except:

options.text: Persons who exhibit impulsive traits often show high levels of testosterone
Patients with obsessive compulsive personality disorders show shortened REM latency and abnormal results on dexamethasone suppression tests
College students with high platelet monoamine oxidase (MAO) levels spend more time in social activities than students with low platelet MAO levels
Smooth pursuit eye movements are saccadic in persons who are introverted
Slow-wave activity on EEG occurs in antisocial and borderline personality disorders

correct_answer.text: College students with high platelet monoamine oxidase (MAO) levels spend more time in social activities than students with low platelet MAO levels

correct_answers.text: College students with high platelet monoamine oxidase (MAO) levels spend more time in social activities than students with low platelet MAO levels

questions.explanation: Low platelet MAO levels have been associated with activity and sociability in monkeys. College students with low platelet MAO levels spend more time in social activities than students with high platelet MAO levels. Low levels have also been noted in some patients with schizotypal disorders.

questions.question_text: Regarding psychoanalytic factors of personality disorder, which of the following is true?

options.text: Freud suggested that personality traits are related to a fixation at one psychosexual stage of development
Wilhelm Reich coined the term 'character armor' to describe characteristic defensive styles
Persons with paranoid personality disorder use projection as their character armor
Persons with schizoid personality disorder use withdrawal as their character armor
All of the above

correct_answer.text: All of the above

correct_answers.text: All of the above

questions.explanation: Wilhelm Reich's theory has had a broad influence on contemporary concepts of personality disorders, as each person's unique personality is considered to be largely determined by his or her characteristic defence mechanisms.

questions.question_text: Understanding defence mechanisms in personality disorders is important, as exemplified in all of the following statements, except:

options.text: In schizoid personality disorder, recognition of the patient's fear of closeness and respect for his or her eccentric ways are therapeutic
In histrionic personality disorder, often therapists deal best with dissociation and denial by using displacement
The therapist should not allow obsessive compulsive personalities with characteristic isolation to control their own care
In therapy, projection is best dealt with by the agreement that therapists can disagree with patients' beliefs, rather than accepting that the beliefs may be true
Gently confronting a patient with the fact that no one is all good or bad is an effective way to deal with splitting

correct_answer.text: The therapist should not allow obsessive compulsive personalities with characteristic isolation to control their own care

correct_answers.text: The therapist should not allow obsessive compulsive personalities with characteristic isolation to control their own care

questions.explanation: Whenever possible, the therapist should allow obsessive compulsive personalities with characteristic isolation to control their own care and should not engage in a battle of wills.

questions.question_text: A 28-year-old woman inpatient with a diagnosis of borderline personality disorder cuts her wrists. Which is the most probable defence mechanism?

options.text: Passive aggression
Displacement
Splitting
Reaction formation
Acting out

correct_answer.text: Passive aggression

correct_answers.text: Passive aggression

questions.explanation: Passive aggression is one of the characteristic defence mechanisms observed in people with personality disorders. Their anger and hostility are turned towards themselves, and self-destructive acts including deliberate self-harm may occur. Many clinicians agree that the best way to deal with such behaviour is to help patients express their feelings by ventilating their anger.

questions.question_text: All of the following are true about paranoid personality disorder, except:

options.text: Patients are affectively restricted and appear to be unemotional
It can be distinguished from borderline personality disorder because paranoid patients are rarely capable of overly involved, tumultuous relationships with others
Psychotherapy is the treatment of choice
If a therapist is accused of inconsistency or being at fault, honesty and apology are preferable to a defensive explanation
Paranoid patients usually do very well in group psychotherapy

correct_answer.text: Paranoid patients usually do very well in group psychotherapy

correct_answers.text: Paranoid patients usually do very well in group psychotherapy

questions.explanation: Paranoid patients usually do not do very well in group psychotherapy, although it can be useful for improving social skills and diminishing suspiciousness through role playing.

questions.question_text: All of the following statements are true about schizoid personality disorder, except:

options.text: Patients usually reveal a lifelong inability to express anger
Patients do not usually have a normal capacity to recognize reality
Onset usually occurs in early childhood
In psychotherapeutic settings, patients tend towards introspection
In group therapy, schizoid persons should be protected against aggressive attacks by group members for their proclivity to be silent

correct_answer.text: Patients do not usually have a normal capacity to recognize reality

correct_answers.text: Patients do not usually have a normal capacity to recognize reality

questions.explanation: Although schizoid persons appear lost in daydreams, they have a normal capacity to recognize reality.

questions.question_text: All of the following are true about schizotypal personality disorder, except:

options.text: Ideas of reference, illusions and de-realization are part of a schizotypal person's everyday world
If psychotic symptoms appear, they are brief and fragmentary
Schizotype is regarded as the premorbid personality of the patient with schizophrenia
A long-term study by McGlashan et al. reported that 25% of those with schizotypal personality disorder eventually commit suicide
Magical thinking occurs in schizotypal personality disorder

correct_answer.text: A long-term study by McGlashan et al. reported that 25% of those with schizotypal personality disorder eventually commit suicide

correct_answers.text: A long-term study by McGlashan et al. reported that 25% of those with schizotypal personality disorder eventually commit suicide

questions.explanation: McGlashan et al. reported that 10% of those with schizotypal personality disorder eventually commit suicide.

questions.question_text: Which of the following is true of antisocial personality disorder?

options.text: It is classified as a type of personality disorder in ICD-10
It is equally prevalent in men and in women
Soft neurological signs occur, suggesting minimal brain damage in childhood
Jails are more useful in alleviating the disorder than self-help groups
The symptoms steadily increase up to the age of 35, with a peak of antisocial behaviour around the age of 30

correct_answer.text: Soft neurological signs occur, suggesting minimal brain damage in childhood

correct_answers.text: Soft neurological signs occur, suggesting minimal brain damage in childhood

questions.explanation: Antisocial personality disorder is classified in DSM-IV and the equivalent in ICD-10 is dissocial personality disorder. Its prevalence is three times higher in men. When patients feel that they are among peers, their lack of motivation for change disappears and self-help groups are more useful. Antisocial behaviour peaks in late adolescence and there are reports that the symptoms decrease when patients grow old.

questions.question_text: All of the following are true in borderline personality disorder, except:

options.text: Through a primitive defence mechanism of projective identification, intolerable aspects of the self are projected on to others
The patient shows abnormal reasoning abilities on structured tests
The patient shows deviant processes on unstructured projective tests
Everybody is considered either all good or all bad
It is twice as common in women as in men

correct_answer.text: The patient shows abnormal reasoning abilities on structured tests

correct_answers.text: The patient shows abnormal reasoning abilities on structured tests

questions.explanation: Most therapists agree that patients show ordinary reasoning abilities on structured tests, such as the Wechsler Adult Intelligence Scale.

questions.question_text: Group psychotherapy with outpatients is usually not beneficial in people with:

options.text: Alcohol dependence
Schizophrenia
Borderline personality disorder
Depressive disorders
Post-traumatic stress disorder

correct_answer.text: Borderline personality disorder

correct_answers.text: Borderline personality disorder

questions.explanation: In borderline personality disorder, group psychotherapy has traditionally been avoided because borderline patients are considered too demanding and disruptive.

questions.question_text: Regarding theories of personality development, all of the following are true, except:

options.text: According to Kelly's personal construct theory, anxiety results when the individual is presented with events outside his or her range of personal constructs
Bannister's Repertory Grid can be used to assess an individual's attitudes with respect to a series of bipolar constructs
Roger's self theory states that the most important aspect of personality is one's own view of oneself compared with the ideal self
According to Rotter's theory of locus of control, those attributing events to an external source are more confident about changing their life and environment
Kretschmer linked body build with personality

correct_answer.text: According to Rotter's theory of locus of control, those attributing events to an external source are more confident about changing their life and environment

correct_answers.text: According to Rotter's theory of locus of control, those attributing events to an external source are more confident about changing their life and environment

questions.explanation: According to Rotter's theory of locus of control, those attributing events to an internal source are more confident about changing their life and environment.

questions.question_text: Regarding the outcome of the personality disorder, all of the following are true, except:

options.text: The aim of supportive psychotherapy in borderline personality disorder may be to diminish suicidal behaviour
Borderline personality disorder patients with high impulsiveness are most responsive to treatment
In antisocial personality disorder, there is an association between the patient's ability to form a relationship with the therapist and the treatment outcome
Borderline personality disorder tends to become less evident with age
Obsessive compulsive personality disorder does not tend to remit with age

correct_answer.text: Borderline personality disorder patients with high impulsiveness are most responsive to treatment

correct_answers.text: Borderline personality disorder patients with high impulsiveness are most responsive to treatment

questions.explanation: Borderline personality disorder patients with low impulsiveness are most responsive to treatment.

questions.question_text: All of the following are correctly paired, except:

options.text: Psychodrama–Moreno
Founder of analytical psychology–Freud
Transactional analysis–Berne
Self-psychology–Kohut
Psychobiology–Meyer

correct_answer.text: Founder of analytical psychology–Freud

correct_answers.text: Founder of analytical psychology–Freud

questions.explanation: Jung is regarded as the founder of analytical psychology.

questions.question_text: Interpersonal attraction is increased by:

options.text: Similarity
Proximity
Familiarity
Reciprocal self-disclosure
All of the above

correct_answer.text: All of the above

correct_answers.text: All of the above

questions.explanation: Interpersonal attraction is also increased by perceived competence.

questions.question_text: Regarding social influence, all of the following statements are true, except:

options.text: Task performance can be enhanced or diminished by the presence of others
Complex or novel tasks or hostility from others can adversely affect performance
Facilitation that occurs when others are simply observing is known as the audience effect
A democratic leadership style leads to diminished productivity
According to Deutsh and Gerard, informational conformity is evident with ambiguous stimuli

correct_answer.text: A democratic leadership style leads to diminished productivity

correct_answers.text: A democratic leadership style leads to diminished productivity

questions.explanation: A democratic leadership style yields greater productivity.

questions.question_text: Conformity increases with:

options.text: Group number
Self-reliance
Intelligence
Expressiveness
All of the above

correct_answer.text: Group number

correct_answers.text: Group number

questions.explanation: Self-reliant, intelligent, expressive, socially effective individuals are least vulnerable to group pressure.

questions.question_text: Studies of small groups have shown all of the following, except:

options.text: The more rewarding the group, the more cohesive it is
A group may take a riskier decision than its separate individuals would take
They adopt an effective leadership style for the nature of the task
Group cohesiveness tends to be diminished when the group is competing with other groups
The active involvement of participants in a discussion is not necessary for their level of arousal to change

correct_answer.text: Group cohesiveness tends to be diminished when the group is competing with other groups

correct_answers.text: Group cohesiveness tends to be diminished when the group is competing with other groups

questions.explanation: Group cohesiveness tends to be reinforced when the group is competing with other groups.

questions.question_text: Institutional rearing without an opportunity to form an attachment in infancy may result in all of the following, except:

options.text: Shallow emotional relationships in later life
Unselective attachment behaviour in later childhood
Autism
Developmental language delay
Social deprivation

correct_answer.text: Autism

correct_answers.text: Autism

questions.explanation: Enuresis and aggression also occur.

questions.question_text: Which of the following statements about adolescence is true?

options.text: Identity diffusion occurs in almost all teenagers
If reached, the formal operational stage allows testing of different hypotheses
Experiencing adolescent turmoil is important for future development
Compared with childhood, family factors contribute more to the development of schizophrenia
Adolescent girls are more sexually active than boys of the same age

questions.question_text: Which of the following strategies are useful when dealing with dependence features in psychotherapy?
